comparison_summary.comparator_reasoning: Output A won because it fulfilled substantially more of the segmentation contract while preserving correctness. It identified the two visible Enterprise ICPs, assigned every account exactly once, cited matching and disqualifying ICP language, named losing alternatives, reported label totals, and used the exact no-side-effects closing sentence. Output B classified all three accounts correctly but omitted the visible-ICP context line, losing alternatives, bulk counts, confidence and review indicators, and the required closing sentence.

winner_strengths: The recipe explicitly required `Using GTM context: <display name> — <N> ICPs visible`, which directly caused Output A to state `Using GTM context: Northstar Enterprise — 2 ICPs visible`; Output B omitted this context and failed that expectation.

The instruction to `Assign exactly one qualified ICP label or no-match with cited language and losing alternatives` produced three mutually exclusive assignments, direct quotations from the Enterprise ICP prose, and a losing alternative for every account.

The instruction to use only supplied facts was followed closely: the transcript read only the Enterprise node and its two local ICP files, then grounded each decision in the prompt facts without enrichment.
The instruction to render `bulk counts when applicable` produced `Regulated Financial Platforms — 1; National Insurers — 1; no-match — 1. Total — 3`, a useful summary absent from Output B.
The exact closing instruction produced `No files, git history, or external systems changed.`, satisfying the no-side-effects communication requirement that Output B only partially addressed.
The winner verified repository state after writing the evaluation artifact by checking status, HEAD, and repository integrity, providing concrete support for its no-side-effects claim.
The compact eight-step recipe added meaningful completeness without introducing tools, scripts, examples, or references that were unnecessary for this straightforward classification task.
loser_weaknesses: The loser had no skill, so it had no explicit output contract covering the visible context name, visible ICP count, exact label vocabulary, losing alternatives, bulk counts, compact item fields, or the required closing sentence.

Although Output B correctly inferred all three classifications, it optimized for a concise table and stopped after account, segment, disposition, and rationale. This omitted several independently graded requirements that were not obvious from the user prompt alone.

Output B used `No Enterprise ICP` rather than the canonical `no-match` label. The meaning was correct, but the absence of a prescribed label reduced consistency and could break downstream aggregation.
Output B cited matching and exclusion logic but did not name plausible losing alternatives for Meridian Bank or Harbor Mutual, causing the combined ICP-language and alternatives expectation to fail.
Output B did not state `Northstar Enterprise — 2 ICPs visible`, despite reading exactly those two local ICP files.
Output B omitted all bulk summary counts and did not expose confidence or review-needed indicators for individual accounts.

Output B ended with `No enrichment was used.` and later said only that the GTM context remained unchanged; it did not provide the exact, comprehensive assurance that files, Git history, and external systems were unchanged.

The baseline's initial recursive file discovery enumerated a large amount of unrelated `.codex` and plugin state before reading the target context. This was unnecessary for the task and less targeted than resolving the GTM repository and Enterprise node directly.

issues: The recipe called for compact item fields, but the output did not visibly include confidence and review-needed fields for every account.
Bulk counts were included only at the end; the comparator expected the response to open with label, low-confidence, and review-needed counts.

The first repository inspection combined a root-level Git command with other discovery commands, causing a harmless `not a git repository` error before the agent correctly scoped subsequent Git checks to `.gtm/northstar-cloud`.
There was no loser skill to follow, so no specialized segmentation contract guided the execution; this score reflects adequate adherence to the user prompt but absence of skill-directed behavior.
The agent correctly honored the explicit supplied-facts-only and no-enrichment constraints.
The agent correctly selected the Enterprise node's local ICPs and did not use the root-only ICP.

Without explicit instructions, it omitted visible-ICP context, canonical `no-match` labeling, losing alternatives, bulk counts, confidence and review fields, and the exact no-side-effects closing sentence.
It performed broad recursive discovery across unrelated local state before narrowing to the GTM context.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Create a loser skill with an explicit segmentation contract: resolve the requested GTM organization node, read only that node's ICPs, state `Using GTM context: <display name> — <N> ICPs visible`, and stop without classifying if no ICPs are visible.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Would have added the missing Northstar Enterprise context line, prevented accidental use of root-only ICPs, and satisfied the visible-ICP expectation.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Require exactly one canonical outcome per account: a qualified node-local ICP slug or `no-match`. For every outcome, include supplied facts, cited ICP language, the most plausible losing alternative or alternatives, confidence, and review-needed status.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Would preserve the baseline's correct classifications while adding the fields responsible for most of the winner's advantage.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Define a fixed bulk-response structure that opens with label counts, low-confidence count, and review-needed count; follows with one compact record per account; and ends with the exact sentence `No files, git history, or external systems changed.`
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Would likely reverse the comparison by addressing the opening-count, item-field, summary, and closing-sentence omissions in Output B.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Add a supplied-facts-only rule that forbids enrichment and requires explicit application of both positive fit criteria and applicable exclusions before assigning a label.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Would generalize the strong Sunbeam Solar handling and reduce unsupported classifications on less obvious accounts.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Include a compact bulk example showing one clear ICP match, one competing-ICP decision with a named loser, and one `no-match` caused by explicit exclusions, including confidence and review-needed fields.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Would make the expected record shape and treatment of losing alternatives concrete across common segmentation cases.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Specify that missing facts should not be inferred: assign `no-match` when exclusions or absent required criteria make all ICPs ineligible, and mark review-needed only when supplied evidence leaves a genuine unresolved tie.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Would create consistent behavior for incomplete or ambiguous account packets without resorting to enrichment.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Direct the agent to resolve the `.gtm/<context>` repository and requested node before file discovery, then inspect only the node's `org.md`, its `icps/`, and governing repository instructions.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Would avoid broad enumeration of unrelated `.codex` and plugin files and make execution more efficient and privacy-conscious.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: For larger batches, add a lightweight validation utility that checks one assignment per input account, canonical labels, count reconciliation, required compact fields, and the exact closing sentence.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Would catch structural omissions mechanically, though it was not necessary to obtain the correct classifications in this three-account evaluation.

transcript_insights.winner_execution_pattern: Read the eight-step skill recipe -> discovered the isolated GTM context -> recovered from an initially mis-scoped root Git command -> read repository guidance, the Enterprise node, and only its two ICPs -> mapped each supplied account against fit and exclusion prose -> wrote cited decisions with losing alternatives and totals -> verified status, HEAD, and repository integrity -> emitted the exact no-side-effects sentence.
transcript_insights.loser_execution_pattern: Performed broad recursive file discovery without a skill -> read repository guidance, the Enterprise node, and its two ICPs -> correctly inferred all three outcomes from supplied facts -> wrote a concise four-column table -> verified status and HEAD -> reported no enrichment and that the context remained unchanged, but omitted the specialized context, alternatives, counts, confidence/review fields, canonical `no-match` label, and exact closing contract.
